item.title: The prompt
item.description:
You type in one place. The first characters decide what runs. The accent caret follows the insertion point as you edit the line.

flowchart LR
 line["The line you type"]:::step
 shell["Shell"]:::out
 endpoint["@endpoint"]:::step
 tool["@tool"]:::store
 skill["/ skill"]:::gate
 model{"@chat # @agent"}:::gate

 line --> shell
 line --> endpoint
 line --> tool
 line --> skill
 line --> model

 classDef store fill:#134e4a,stroke:#5eead4,stroke-width:2px,color:#f4fbfa
 classDef gate fill:#FFC131,stroke:#b45309,stroke-width:2px,color:#1a1404
 classDef step fill:#0f766e,stroke:#99f6e4,stroke-width:2px,color:#f4fbfa
 classDef out fill:#155e75,stroke:#67e8f9,stroke-width:2px,color:#f4fbfa
 linkStyle 0,2 stroke:#5eead4,stroke-width:2.5px
 linkStyle 1 stroke:#67e8f9,stroke-width:2.5px
 linkStyle 3,4 stroke:#FFC131,stroke-width:2.5px
You type What runs
git status The tab’s shell. Output streams in. cd and export carry to the next line on bash, zsh, sh, and PowerShell
@endpoint List users A saved HTTP call
@tool search --query tea An MCP tool on a server connected to this tab
/explain how to make tea A skill from skills.yaml
@chat why was that empty? The tab’s model, with recent scrollback. It can call this tab’s MCP tools and saved endpoints; you approve each call
Agent on, then why was that empty? The same chat, without typing @chat. A line that starts with @ still runs
# find files over 100 MB here The model writes one command into the prompt. You press Enter
@history The history overlay for this tab

@ opens the commands palette. / opens the skills palette. Both filter as you type. In the commands palette, exact and leading name matches appear before other name matches, and all name matches appear before description matches. Built-in @ actions are listed in Commands. Entries from commands.yaml follow them. @history is always first and is not a YAML entry.

item.title: Shells
item.description:
A line that is not an @ command or a / skill runs in the tab’s shell. One command runs at a time per tab. Output streams in while it runs. Ctrl+C stops that command and everything it started.

Which shells link

Settings → Shell picks the shell for every tab that has not chosen its own, from the ones installed here.

Platform Choices
macOS and Linux bash, zsh, fish, sh, PowerShell 7
Windows Windows PowerShell, PowerShell 7, Command Prompt, Git Bash, WSL

Right-click a tab, then Shell, to choose one for that tab, or Default to follow Settings. The header shows the active tab’s shell. @shell opens that shell as an interactive terminal.

item.title: Tabs and splits
item.description:
Each tab is its own session: scrollback, folder, history, MCP servers, and OpenAI connection. Switching tabs leaves a running command where it is.

Add, rename, close link

+ adds a tab in the start folder. Right-click for Rename and Change colour. Middle-click, ×, or Close removes the tab. Closing the last tab resets it.

Ctrl+Tab moves to the next tab. Ctrl+Shift+Tab moves to the previous one. Both wait while a palette or a dialog is open.

item.title: Interactive terminal
item.description:
Most lines are non-interactive: the app starts the shell, streams the output, and returns to the prompt. A program that needs a keyboard opens a pseudo-terminal in the tab instead. On Windows that terminal is ConPTY. The screen is drawn with xterm.js.

These open a terminal on their own:

  • Editors and pagers
  • ssh and sudo
  • top
  • git commit without -m, and git add -p
  • docker exec -it
  • A REPL started without a script, such as python, node, or psql mydb

@shell opens an interactive shell in the tab until you type exit.

item.title: History and plain English
item.description:
Command history link

↑ and ↓ cycle the commands on this tab when no palette is open. The app keeps the last 500 in command_history.json in the app data folder. Each entry is the command and at, Unix epoch milliseconds. An older file that was a plain list of strings is migrated on load (at: 0 shows as an unknown time).

[
 { "command": "git status", "at": 1727900000000 }
]

The active tab’s history is the one ↑ and ↓ and @history use. It is mirrored to that file when commands run.

item.title: Find and export
item.description:
Find in the scrollback link

Cmd+F on macOS, or Ctrl+F on Windows and Linux, opens a search box over the active tab. Every match is highlighted. The current one is filled in the accent colour, with a count such as 3 of 12.

Enter and Shift+Enter, or the arrows, step through matches and wrap at either end. Aa matches case. Esc closes the box. New output is searched as it arrives.
